data.text:
🚨🚨JUST IN 🚨 

🇵🇭 Tragic Landfill Collapse in Philippines Leaves One Dead, Dozens Missing

A big accident happened at a landfill in the central part of the Philippines, where part of the waste site fell down, killing at least one person and leaving many others lost under the rubble. Rescue teams are working hard to find and save people.

The collapse took place late on Thursday afternoon, January 8, at around 4:17 p.m., at the Binaliw landfill in Cebu City. There were about 110 workers there when it happened. So far, officials say one person has died, and 34 others are still missing. The falling waste damaged some buildings nearby that belonged to the landfill company.

Right away, help came from many groups. Police, firefighters, soldiers, and disaster teams rushed to the site with ambulances, fire trucks, and bright lights to work through the night. They are searching for survivors and checking what went wrong.

Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival shared on Facebook that rescue work is still going on. He said the city is teaming up with national groups and the landfill bosses to handle the crisis and support the families of those hurt or missing.

No one knows yet why the landfill collapsed, but experts might look into things like too much rain or poor building. This kind of event shows how important it is to keep waste sites safe, especially in places with lots of people nearby.

As the search continues, locals and families wait for news. We will share more updates as they come. If you live near Cebu, stay away from the area and follow safety tips from officials.

Source: Reuters
